title: GE's Lazarus Moment: How Larry Culp Orchestrated an Unbelievable $689 Billion Comeback
summary: Once teetering on the brink of bankruptcy, industrial titan General Electric has been stunningly resurrected under the leadership of CEO Larry Culp. His relentless focus on operational excellence and strategic divestitures transformed a near-collapsed conglomerate into a $689 billion powerhouse.
content:
Just a few short years ago, the iconic General Electric, a cornerstone of American industry for over a century, seemed irrevocably doomed. The sentiment was palpable, even among the most seasoned investors. “I was sure GE was going to file for Chapter 11,” confessed activist investor Nelson Peltz recently, echoing widespread fears that the sprawling conglomerate was heading for the corporate graveyard.

Then came Larry Culp. In 2018, Culp took the helm, inheriting a company mired in debt, complex operations, and a plummeting stock price. What followed was an astonishing display of corporate surgical precision. Culp embarked on a radical, yet disciplined, strategy to dismantle the bloated empire, shedding underperforming assets, aggressively paying down debt, and sharpening the focus on its core strengths: aviation, healthcare, and power.

This wasn't merely a clean-up job; it was a wholesale reinvention. Culp’s tenure saw the strategic spin-offs of GE HealthCare and GE Vernova (its power and renewables business), transforming the once-diversified behemoth into three independent, publicly traded companies. This bold segmentation not only unlocked immense shareholder value but also allowed each entity to pursue its distinct market opportunities with renewed agility.

Today, the collective market capitalization of these three entities stands at an eye-watering $689 billion. This remarkable turnaround isn't just a testament to Culp's leadership and unwavering vision; it's a masterclass in corporate restructuring, proving that even the most formidable challenges can be overcome with decisive action and an unyielding commitment to fundamental business principles. GE's journey from near-collapse to a multi-billion-dollar success story is, as Peltz succinctly put it, "the most amazing rescue I've ever seen."
keyTakeaways: Larry Culp's leadership transformed GE from near-bankruptcy to a collective $689 billion market valuation.
The turnaround involved a strategic dismantling of the conglomerate, focusing on core strengths through spin-offs like GE HealthCare and GE Vernova.
Culp's approach emphasized debt reduction, operational excellence, and sharpening focus, demonstrating a masterclass in corporate restructuring.
author: Shawn Tully
